raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've farmed this land in Quzhou for over 40 years. My father farmed it before me. We grow wheat and corn — everyone here does. The land is flat, the water table is there if you pump for it, and the grain station buys what you grow. Why would I change now?

I have about 10 mu. My son works in Handan city, so it's mostly me and my wife. I can manage 10 mu with some hired help at harvest.

For wheat, I'll plant in early October as always. I use 矮抗58 (Aikang 58) — it's been reliable here for years, I know how it behaves in my fields. I'll rotary-till before planting since the corn stalks need breaking up. I apply base fertilizer before seeding and top-dress at jointing. I irrigate at: winter freeze (越冬水), jointing (拔节水), and heading (灌浆水). Three times is what my fields need. My neighbor skipped the winter irrigation two years ago and regretted it.

Right after wheat harvest in June I plant corn. Zhengdan 958 hybrid — cheap, available at the co-op, good yield. I seed straight into the stubble without tilling, saves time and my back. Summer rains help but I'll irrigate at tasseling if it's dry like last year.

I don't like to change things that work. My yields aren't fancy but they're steady.
